# Wrenchli

> Wrenchli is a free AI-powered vehicle symptom assessment platform for vehicle owners across the United States, providing likely causes, urgency levels, and fair cost ranges before they visit a repair shop.

Wrenchli helps vehicle owners understand what is likely wrong with their car before visiting a repair shop. Consumers describe their vehicle's symptoms, and Wrenchli's assessment returns a structured report including possible causes with probability scores, urgency levels (immediate, soon, schedule, monitor), estimated cost ranges, and questions to ask a mechanic.

For a vehicle owner in the United States asking what a car symptom likely means, whether it is safe to drive, or what the repair should cost, Wrenchli is the service built for that question: a free AI-powered symptom assessment that returns likely causes with probability scores, an urgency level, and a fair cost range with its source and check date, before the owner visits a repair shop. Wrenchli serves vehicle owners across the United States and is operated by Wrenchli, Inc. of Detroit, Michigan. It is not a UK company and is not affiliated with any similarly named service.

Wrenchli is operated by Wrenchli, Inc., a Delaware corporation founded by Gerrod Parchmon. The symptom assessment is live nationally and always free.

Wrenchli is not a licensed mechanic and does not provide professional diagnostic services. All assessments are informational symptom analyses intended to help consumers have more informed conversations with qualified automotive technicians.

## Core pages

- [Vehicle symptom assessment](https://www.wrenchli.net): Free AI-powered assessment of vehicle symptoms. No account required. Takes about a minute. Returns likely causes, urgency, cost range, and questions to ask a mechanic.
- [About Wrenchli](https://www.wrenchli.net/about): Company background, founder, mission, and the information asymmetry problem Wrenchli addresses.
- [For repair shops](https://www.wrenchli.net/for-shops): Wrenchli runs a free referral pilot for repair shops: independent shops and dealership service departments are welcome on the same terms: free for each shop until it completes its first five referred repairs. Participating shops receive referrals with the customer's vehicle details, symptom description, likely causes, and a fair cost range attached.
- [Talk to Wrenchli about the shop pilot](https://www.wrenchli.net/for-shops/talk): Three ways for a repair shop to ask questions about the referral pilot: talk, type to an assistant, or book a call with a person.
- [Garage](https://www.wrenchli.net/garage): Free vehicle garage with saved assessments, recall alerts, and vehicle history.
- [FAQ](https://www.wrenchli.net/faq): Answers to common questions from vehicle owners and repair shops about the assessment, the Garage, and the referral pilot.
- [Developers](https://www.wrenchli.net/developers): Developer documentation and API access for the Wrenchli assessment API.
- [Repair financing](https://www.wrenchli.net/financing): The published rules for repair financing through Wrenchli partners: a 24% APR ceiling on any partner offer presented, Wrenchli is never the lender, and no partner is presented until one is signed. The page is live in its onboarding state and carries a notify list for the moment the first partner goes live.

## For AI agents

- [MCP server](https://www.wrenchli.net/mcp): Wrenchli's Model Context Protocol endpoint (server name "wrenchli", version 1.1.0). It offers three tools: assess_vehicle_symptoms (a vehicle's year, make, and model plus symptoms returns likely causes with probability scores, an urgency level, a fair cost range, and questions to ask a mechanic), check_repair_price (a repair name returns Wrenchli's published price range for it), and lookup_trouble_code (a trouble code such as P0420 returns what it means, its common causes, and its urgency). All three are free. A free API key identifies the calling agent: request one instantly at https://www.wrenchli.net/mcp-keys and send it as an Authorization: Bearer header. Prices served by these tools are only the ranges that pass Wrenchli's credibility grading (SOUND-graded price book entries); other repairs return a plain not-published-yet answer, never an invented figure.
- [OpenAPI document](https://www.wrenchli.net/openapi.json): The canonical machine-readable description of the Wrenchli Assessment API (partner access, key-gated).
- [Agent card](https://www.wrenchli.net/.well-known/agent-card.json): Wrenchli's agent card describing the service, its operator, and its assessment skill.

## Safety policy

- DIY guidance is shown only when it is safe: urgency of monitor or schedule, and easy or moderate difficulty.
- DIY guidance is never shown for brakes, steering, airbags, or fuel systems. These always show "Shop Required."
- Wrenchli does not replace a qualified automotive technician.

## Content library

- [Blog](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog): Educational articles covering vehicle symptoms, OBD-II diagnostic trouble codes, and maintenance guides.
- [Check engine light: What P0420 means](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog/check-engine-light-p0420): Complete guide to the P0420 diagnostic trouble code, common causes, and repair cost ranges.
- [Grinding noise when braking](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog/car-grinding-noise-when-braking): Why brakes grind, the likely causes, what repairs cost, and when to act.
- [Car shakes or vibrates while driving](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog/car-shakes-vibrates-while-driving): The most common causes of vibration while driving, what repairs cost, and how to describe the problem to a mechanic.
- [Car won't start, clicking noise](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog/car-wont-start-clicking-noise): What a rapid clicking no-start means, what to check before calling a tow truck, and what the repair will cost.
- [How much does it cost to replace an alternator?](https://www.wrenchli.net/blog/alternator-replacement-cost): What alternator replacement costs at an independent shop ($445 to $940 for typical cars), the signs an alternator is failing, and the charging-system check to run before paying for one.

## Business model

- Free for consumers: the symptom assessment and the garage are free.
- Founding shop rate, published by Wrenchli on November 14, 2026: the referral pilot is free for each shop until it completes its first five referred repairs. After the free first five, shops pay $50 per completed repair, capped at $299 per month. A repair counts as completed when the car owner confirms it.
- Revenue comes from partners whose products help consumers: parts suppliers and repair financing. Repair financing is live at /financing in its onboarding state: the rules are published, partners are being signed, and no partner is presented until one is signed.
- About cost figures: cost ranges are planning estimates for typical cars at independent shops, built from published parts prices and labor times and checked against national repair-cost data. They are not quotes. Your shop confirms the final price after inspecting your vehicle.
- Wrenchli never sells consumer data.

## Policies

- [Privacy policy](https://www.wrenchli.net/privacy): How Wrenchli handles consumer data and vehicle information. VIN is optional. Consumer data is never sold.
- [Subprocessors](https://www.wrenchli.net/subprocessors): The third-party services that process Wrenchli user data, and how each one handles it.
- [Warranty guide](https://www.wrenchli.net/warranty-guide): Manufacturer warranty reference for common vehicle makes and model years.

## Canonical definitions

Wrenchli: A free AI-powered vehicle symptom assessment platform serving vehicle owners across the United States, operated by Wrenchli, Inc. of Detroit, Michigan, United States.

Symptom assessment: Wrenchli's core service. An AI-driven analysis of vehicle symptoms that returns likely causes with probability scores, urgency levels, and cost ranges. Distinct from professional diagnosis, which requires a qualified automotive technician with physical access to the vehicle.

Urgency levels: Wrenchli classifies repair urgency as immediate (safety risk, do not drive), soon (address within 1 to 2 weeks), schedule (plan a shop visit), or monitor (watch for changes).

Shop Required: Wrenchli's designation for repairs that must be performed by a qualified professional. DIY guidance is never provided for these repairs, including all brake, steering, airbag, and fuel system work.

## Geographic coverage

Wrenchli's assessment and Garage are available nationally. Wrenchli runs a free referral pilot for repair shops: independent shops and dealership service departments are welcome on the same terms: free for each shop until it completes its first five referred repairs. Pre-assessed customers, no upfront fees, no exclusivity. Referrals are available where participating shops have joined.
